entries.title: Create and Writing Copilot hide job title and company from users without contact access
entries.summary: Team members whose event role does not grant access to contacts, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors or accounts no longer see participant job titles or company names in **Redraft** output or **Writing Copilot** responses. Names and session roles are still included; only the protected details are withheld. Org admins and roles with contact access continue to receive full attribution.
entries.use_case: Organisations that restrict certain team members (for example, a marketing role with no people access) from viewing contact details can now be confident that Create and the Writing Copilot will not inadvertently expose job titles or company names to those users through generated content.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic; no configuration required. Restricted users will notice that Redraft and Copilot responses no longer include job titles or company names for participants.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about data privacy for team members who should not see speaker or contact details, or when a customer has roles scoped to marketing-only access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with event team roles that have partial contact permissions — common in larger organisations with separate marketing and programme teams.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Create → Redraft or Writing Copilot
internal.gotchas: Drafts already saved by a user who previously had contact access keep their existing text and citation chips; the gate applies only to new drafts, redrafts and Copilot turns going forward.
internal.talk_track: If a team member's role can't read contacts, Create now respects that boundary — they'll see speaker names and session roles in generated content, but not job titles or company names.

entries.title: Credit type details save correctly for common increment values
entries.summary: **Save details** on a credit type's **Details** tab now works for all valid increment values. Previously, common values such as 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 triggered a browser step-mismatch error that silently blocked the save request from being sent.
entries.use_case: Organizers setting up credit types with standard increment values (0.25, 0.5, 1, etc.) can now save changes to the Details tab without the form silently failing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that saving credit type details appears to do nothing, or that changes to the Accreditor or other fields are not persisting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Credit Claiming with credit types that have increments like 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 or 1.
internal.gotchas: The bug only affected the Details tab save; the designation panel (SessionCreditDesignationPanel) was unaffected.
internal.talk_track: A browser validation bug was silently blocking saves on the credit type Details tab for the most common increment values — that is now fixed.

entries.title: Sponsor and exhibitor contact roles are now visible and editable on the group profile
entries.summary: Each contact listed on a sponsor or exhibitor group profile now shows their role as a badge. The row menu includes **Edit role**, which opens a dialog with the default roles and any roles already in use as suggestions; leaving the field empty clears the role. The same badge and edit option appear in the **Sponsor/Exhibitor Profile** sidebar.
entries.use_case: Organizers who collect contact roles through the sponsor or exhibitor intake form can now see those roles at a glance on the group profile and correct or clear them without leaving the page.

cs_action.note: Default on; no enablement needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why roles collected on the intake form were not visible to admins, or wants to manage sponsor/exhibitor contact roles after submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using sponsor or exhibitor intake forms with the contact-role question.
internal.staff_path: Sponsors or Exhibitors → open a group → Contacts tab → row menu → Edit role
internal.gotchas: Roles are saved through the existing PUT /account/:id/contact-relationships endpoint; no new API surface. Requires the matching web-api PR on the same branch.
internal.talk_track: Roles your sponsors filled in on the intake form now show as badges on their profile, and you can edit or clear any role directly from the contacts list.

entries.title: Dispatch: Slack shows as connected and delivers DMs to team members by email when no Slack ID is found
entries.summary: The **Dispatch** editor no longer incorrectly shows "Slack isn't connected" when the Slack roster fails to load — the connection status stays accurate. Team members who have no Slack user ID now receive a direct message looked up by email address automatically; if no match is found, they fall back to email delivery only.
entries.use_case: Teams using Dispatch with Slack were seeing a false "Slack isn't connected" warning and missing DMs to teammates whose Slack IDs weren't stored — both issues are now resolved so every send reaches the right people.

cs_action.note: Default-on fix; no action needed. Affected customers may have already noticed the false warning or missing DMs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Dispatch says Slack is not connected even though Apps → Slack shows it is, or that team members are not receiving Slack DMs from a Dispatch send.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Dispatch with Slack enabled.
internal.gotchas: Team members with no Slack ID and no matching email in the Slack workspace will still fall back to email-only delivery.
internal.talk_track: Dispatch now correctly reads the Slack connection status even when the roster is slow to load, and it looks up teammates by email when their Slack ID isn't on file — so DMs go out reliably.

entries.title: Report exports use the correct sheet name, shared pivot reports match the builder, and contact-profile access is enforced by role
entries.summary: Four user-visible fixes shipped together. **Exported reports** now name the Excel sheet after the report (e.g. "Session Summary") instead of the generic label "Report". **Shared saved reports** that include a pivot now return the same pivoted row count as the report builder, rather than the raw unpivoted rows. **Contact profile** pages at the organization level now require the viewer to be an org member with org access, or to hold a role on one of the org's events that can view Contacts, Speakers, Exhibitors, Sponsors or Accounts — event-only staff (such as Evaluators) who previously slipped through are now correctly denied. A security fix also ensures that **SbQL queries run under impersonation** use the target user's record scope, so contact-rule limits and session-scope restrictions are applied correctly. **Insights** now needs **Can view reports** for event-only team members, and report links from a scheduled report keep the saved pivot.
entries.use_case: Organizers who download reports to Excel no longer have to rename the sheet before sharing. Teams using shared pivot reports can trust that the link delivers the same summarised data they see in the builder. Admins can be confident that event-only staff (e.g. Evaluators) cannot read contact profiles they have no permission to see.

cs_action.note: All four fixes are default-on bug fixes; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their exported Excel sheet is always named 'Report', that a shared pivot link shows more rows than the builder, or that an Evaluator-role user can open contact profiles they should not see.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using report exports, shared saved reports with pivots, or event-only staff roles.
internal.staff_path: Insights → Reports → Download (for sheet name); share a saved pivot report link (for pivot fix); Contacts profile page (for access fix)
internal.gotchas: Event-only staff with has_org_access = false (e.g. Evaluators, custom roles with People off) will now receive a 403 on org-level contact profile pages they could previously open. ~2,500 users on prod are affected. Confirm with the customer that this is the intended behaviour before escalating.
internal.talk_track: We fixed three report accuracy issues and tightened contact-profile access so only people with the right event role can open a contact's org-level profile.

entries.title: All Off / All On buttons now appear only on the Permissions tab and ask for confirmation
entries.summary: The **All Off** and **All On** buttons in the role editor now appear only on the **Permissions** tab, not on the **Fields**, **Statuses** or **Notifications** tabs. Both buttons show a confirmation prompt before applying the change. This prevents accidentally wiping or granting every permission while working on unrelated role settings. The fix applies to both event roles and organization roles.
entries.use_case: Prevents a team admin from accidentally resetting all permissions on a role (such as Co-Chair) while editing its field visibility or notification settings — a mistake that previously wiped carefully configured access without warning.

cs_action.note: Default-on bug fix; no action needed. Relevant if a customer reports that a role's permissions were wiped — this fix prevents recurrence.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a role lost all its permissions unexpectedly, or asks whether bulk-toggle is safe to use.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who manages custom roles with fine-grained permissions, especially those with Co-Chair or vendor roles.
internal.gotchas: ILTA had a Co-Chair role wiped by this bug before the fix. If a customer reports a similar incident, the fix is now live and a confirmation prompt guards future changes.
internal.talk_track: All Off and All On now only appear on the Permissions tab and ask you to confirm before applying, so there is no risk of accidentally clearing a role while adjusting field or notification settings.

entries.title: Review plan fixes: AI persona exports, closed-allocation visibility, multi-file fields, plan monitor speed, and reviewer thread notifications
entries.summary: Five fixes to review plans ship together. **Grade**, **Score Summary** and **Cumulative** exports now include submissions assigned to AI personas (previously dropped). Submissions whose allocations were all closed by a per-reviewer limit now appear in the **Plan Monitor** as **Closed: x of N** instead of disappearing. Multi-file submission fields show all uploaded files to reviewers in the portal (previously only the first file). The **Plan Monitor** page loads significantly faster on large plans. Reviewers who participated in an earlier round no longer receive email notifications for messages posted in later rounds they are not assigned to.
entries.use_case: Organizers running AI-assisted reviews can now export complete grade and score data without missing persona-assigned submissions, and reviewers in the portal see all files attached to a submission rather than just the first one.

cs_action.note: All five fixes are default-on bug fixes; no action required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports missing rows in review exports, a submission disappearing from the plan monitor when review limits are in use, reviewers seeing only one file when multiple were uploaded, slow plan monitor page loads on large events, or reviewers from ended rounds getting emailed about new messages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using v2 review plans, especially those using AI Screener personas, per-reviewer review limits, multi-file submission fields, large plans, or multi-round reviewer threads.
internal.gotchas: The multi-file fix returns an array for multi-file fields; single-file fields keep the existing single-object shape the portal already reads. The notification fix only drops reviewer participants whose live v2 assignments are all in rounds past their end date; v1/org plans and @mentions are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Wave 4 of the review sweep closes five QA-bounced issues: complete exports when AI personas are used, correct monitor counts under review limits, all files visible to reviewers, faster monitor page loads, and quieter email notifications for reviewers whose rounds have ended.

entries.title: Portal session dates now follow the portal's language and date-style setting
entries.summary: Session date labels throughout the speaker portal — on the home page, **My Participation**, task group headers and the session detail view — now respect the portal's **Language** setting and the event's **Record Settings** date style. German portals show dates in German order (e.g. "Do., 22. Apr., 10:15 - 11:00 CEST"); English portals on events configured with a European date style show day-before-month order (e.g. "Mon 19 Oct, 14:00") instead of US order.

where.path: Portals → [portal name] → (home, My Participation, task groups, session detail)

entries.use_case: Events running non-English portals or using a European date format no longer show speakers dates in the wrong locale order — German speakers see German-formatted dates, and EU-style English events show day-before-month throughout the portal.

cs_action.note: English portals on events where Record Settings has advocacy_datetime_format = 'eu', or where no date style is set on a 24-hour event, will change from US-style ('Mon, Oct 19th, 14:00') to EU-style ('Mon 19 Oct, 14:00') automatically. Heads-up for any customer who has screenshotted or documented their portal date format.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that portal dates are in the wrong language or wrong day/month order, or when onboarding a non-US event that uses a European date style.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running a non-English portal or an English portal on an event configured with a European date style.
internal.staff_path: Event → Record Settings → date style; Portal → Language setting
internal.gotchas: English portals on 24-hour events with no explicit date style set will silently switch to EU order (day before month). This is the correct behaviour but may surprise customers who were used to the old US default.
internal.talk_track: Dates in the portal now match the language and date style you've already configured — no extra setup needed.

entries.title: Swoogo sync summary shows Registration ID counts and unmatched or ambiguous registrants
entries.summary: The Swoogo sync summary now has a **Swoogo Registration IDs** section with the counts written, and warnings for registrants that matched no contact or matched more than one. Leaving **Version** empty in **Event Settings** no longer breaks every sync.
entries.use_case: Organizers who write Swoogo Registration IDs back to contacts can see exactly which registrants were skipped and why.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why some Swoogo registrants have no Registration ID on their contact.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Swoogo and write-back on.
internal.gotchas: Registrants only match on email address; the summary lists the ones that did not. Needs Swoogo registrants whose emails match contacts to show counts.
internal.talk_track: The sync now tells you which registrants it could not match, instead of leaving you to guess.

entries.title: Email Campaigns: Add unsubscribe works and shows what went wrong
entries.summary: **Add unsubscribe** on **Settings → Unsubscribes** now saves the contact you add, and the dialog shows the reason when it cannot.

where.path: Communications → Email Campaigns → Settings → Unsubscribes → Add unsubscribe

entries.use_case: Organizers can honor an opt-out they received by email or phone straight away.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports Add unsubscribe doing nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Email Campaigns customers.
internal.staff_path: Communications → Email Campaigns → Settings → Unsubscribes → Add unsubscribe
internal.gotchas: The button failed silently before; no data was lost.
internal.talk_track: You can add an unsubscribe by hand again, and you see the error if it fails.

entries.title: Speakers you hide no longer appear on share cards or in Dispatch
entries.summary: A speaker hidden from the public listing in the session editor or run of show is now also left off **share cards**, **Dispatch** posts and embeds.

where.path: Program → Sessions → session → hide speaker (eye icon)

entries.use_case: Organizers can hide a speaker once and trust every public surface to respect it.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer saw a hidden speaker on a share card or Dispatch post.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy and Dispatch customers.
internal.staff_path: Program → Sessions → session → hide speaker (eye icon)
internal.gotchas: Rows hidden before the fix are corrected by a one-time data update that Josh runs; until then a few older sessions may still show.
internal.talk_track: Hide a speaker once and it holds everywhere.

entries.title: Media upload, playback and download work for EU events
entries.summary: Uploading, playing back and downloading media, including thumbnails, transcripts, podcast audio and clip downloads, now works for events in the EU.
entries.use_case: Organizers with EU events can upload and use recordings and files like everyone else.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An EU customer could not upload or play media.
internal.who_should_get_it: EU customers.
internal.gotchas: No setting involved. Do not describe storage regions to customers.
internal.talk_track: Media now works end to end for EU events.

entries.title: Insights and Report Builder include AI persona reviews
entries.summary: Review data in **Insights** and **Report Builder** now includes reviews by AI personas, named after the persona.
entries.use_case: Review reports and Insights answers match what the plan monitor and exports already show.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer notices persona reviews missing from a review report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who enroll Screener personas.
internal.gotchas: Before this, only reviews by people appeared in Insights and Report Builder.
internal.talk_track: Persona reviews now show up in reports under the persona name.

entries.title: Portal subsession panel shows and edits Tags, Language, Track and Level
entries.summary: The subsession panel in the speaker portal now shows and edits **Tags**, **Language**, **Track** and **Level** when the portal shows those fields.
entries.use_case: Submitters can see and fix a subsession's classification from the portal.

cs_action.note: Default-on change; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says subsession tags are missing in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with subsessions.
internal.gotchas: Only shown when the portal's session field configuration includes the field.
internal.talk_track: Subsessions now carry their tags, language, track and level in the portal.

entries.title: Speaker Interest Form dashboard now shows a descriptive page title and correct heading hierarchy
entries.summary: The browser tab and page title for the org-level **Speaker Interest Forms** dashboard now reads "Speaker Interest Forms | {org} | Sessionboard" instead of the generic "Sessionboard". Section headings on the page are also promoted from h3 to h2, matching the rest of the admin shell and improving screen-reader navigation.
entries.use_case: Teams using assistive technology or browser tab management can now immediately identify the Interest Forms dashboard by its title, without having to look at the page content.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Only relevant if a customer reports accessibility or tab-title issues on the Interest Forms dashboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Speaker CRM interest forms.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the Interest Forms dashboard page title includes the organization name for easier tab and screen-reader identification.

entries.title: Subsession panels in portals now show Tags, Language, Track and Level
entries.summary: Tags, **Language**, **Track** and **Level** fields now appear in the portal's subsession detail panel and its edit form. Previously only **Title**, **Status**, dates, **Format** and **Description** were passed through, so those fields were always blank for subsessions. Fields still appear only when the portal's session field configuration shows them.
entries.use_case: Speakers managing subsessions in their portal can now see and edit Tags, Language, Track and Level without having to ask an organizer to make those changes in the admin.

cs_action.note: Default on; no action needed. Fields only appear if the portal's session field config already shows them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Tags, Language, Track or Level are missing from subsession panels in the portal, or speakers cannot edit those fields on a subsession.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using subsessions with portals who exposes Tags, Language, Track or Level in their session field config.
internal.gotchas: Fields only appear if the portal's session field configuration is set to show them — the fix does not override that setting.
internal.talk_track: Subsession panels in the portal now pass through the same metadata fields as parent sessions, so speakers can view and edit Tags, Language, Track and Level without admin intervention.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note which session fields are available in the subsession detail panel and edit form within a portal.

entries.title: Agent pages: "More like this" rail and approved clip pages on webinar recording pages
entries.summary: Webinar recording pages on agent-powered sites now include a **More like this** rail of related recordings, ranked by shared tags, speakers and transcript similarity. Each recording's approved clips appear in a **Watch clips** rail, and every clip opens its own page in the site layout with a **Watch next** list of the other clips. Recording cards also pull the current description, tags, poster image and duration directly from the media record, so edits made in **Media** are reflected immediately without re-publishing the gallery.
entries.use_case: Organizers running on-demand webinar libraries get automatic "More like this" recommendations and a clip rail on every recording page, keeping viewers watching longer without any manual curation. Clips that speakers or organizers have approved appear as standalone pages that can be linked, shared and indexed by search engines.

cs_action.note: Delivered automatically to any org with Content Galleries and an agent-powered site; no toggle required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to surface related recordings or share individual clips from their on-demand library.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Content Galleries with agent-powered webinar pages and who have approved clips via send_content_kits or review_content.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Content Galleries → (open a gallery site)
internal.gotchas: Clip pages only appear when the site has a clips route bound; clips must have status: ready, review_status: approved, and a live render. The existing /clip/:id share page is separate and is not used here.
internal.talk_track: Your recording pages now automatically show viewers what to watch next and surface every approved clip as its own shareable page — no extra setup needed.

draft.docs_gap: The clip-pages guide should document the new clips route bind, the automatic "More like this" and "Watch clips" rails on recording pages, the ranking algorithm (tags, speakers, transcript similarity), and how media-level edits propagate to gallery cards without republishing.
draft.why_use_it: Clip pages give every approved clip its own URL in your site's layout, complete with structured data for search engines and a "Watch next" list to keep viewers moving through your content. Use them when you want clips to be discoverable on their own — in search results, social shares or direct links — rather than only inside the full recording page.

entries.title: Keyboard and screen-reader improvements across grids, panels, charts, filters and the sign-up flow
entries.summary: A broad set of accessibility fixes makes Sessionboard usable with a keyboard and screen reader across many surfaces. **Clear** buttons on grid cells now announce the field name (e.g. **Clear Track**); speaker and contact pills open the profile by keyboard; portal task and form status cells are operable with Enter/Space; **ModalSidePanel** retakes focus so Escape always closes it; pipeline cards are no longer a nested button; every switch on record settings and the form builder carries its own label; filter rule columns, conditions and values are named; charts (line, bar, area, pie, scatter, radar) are a single tab stop with arrow-key tooltip navigation and a visible focus ring; untitled admin pages get a descriptive browser title; and the sign-up conversation announces Ask's response when focus lands in the text box.

where.path: Throughout the admin — grids, side panels, pipeline, form builder, filters, charts, sign-up

entries.use_case: Organizations that require WCAG-conformant tools, or whose team members use assistive technology, can now navigate grids, panels, charts and filters entirely by keyboard and have screen readers announce actions and state changes correctly.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer mentions accessibility requirements, a VPAT request, or that a team member uses a screen reader or keyboard-only navigation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with accessibility obligations (government, higher education, healthcare) or whose staff or speakers use assistive technology.
internal.gotchas: This PR covers the admin UI only; the embeds and org-portal accessibility fixes are in separate PRs (SB-11287, SB-11298/SB-11409, SB-11385, SB-11401). A human screen-reader pass is still pending (SB-11305).
internal.talk_track: Keyboard and screen-reader users can now navigate grids, close side panels, read chart data and complete filter rules without a mouse — all default-on with no configuration needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the specific keyboard interactions available in grids (Enter/Space on status cells, arrow keys on charts, named Clear buttons) and note the WCAG criteria each addresses.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard is built to be operable without a mouse. Keyboard users can tab through every interactive control, operate it with Enter or Space, and hear its name and state read aloud by a screen reader. Charts are a single tab stop with arrow-key navigation; filter rules, grid cells and side panels all carry accessible names; and the sign-up conversation announces responses as they arrive. These behaviours let organizers, reviewers, speakers and participants with disabilities use the full product on equal terms.

entries.title: Video portal pages: poster behind the gate, improved gate heading, styled transcript, and visible Watch next cards
entries.summary: Recording pages built with `<sb-portal kind="video">` now show a blurred, dimmed poster image behind the sign-up gate instead of a black box. The gate heading reads **Watch the full recording** with the recording title as a sub-line (a heading you wrote on the form still wins). The transcript renders as a collapsible section with speaker turns grouped, time-code links that seek the player, and a labelled search box. **Watch next** cards — poster, title and length — are now visible as soon as the page loads rather than only after the video ends.
entries.use_case: Visitors who land on a gated recording page now see a preview of the content — the poster, a clear heading, and what to watch next — before they fill in the sign-up form, which reduces drop-off and sets expectations about the recording they are about to watch.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all video portal pages; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their gated recording page looks blank before sign-up, or wants to improve conversion on their on-demand library.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer publishing gated recording pages via sb-portal or Sessionboard Marketing recording pages.
internal.gotchas: Poster resolution depends on what media ingest stored (thumbnail_s3_key). YouTube stills are only used for open (ungated) recordings to avoid leaking the video ID. The client-side seek and transcript search require the matching sessionboard-embeds#154 release.
internal.talk_track: Your recording page now shows a real preview image and a clear call to action before the gate, and visitors can see what to watch next the moment the page loads — no more black box.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the poster fallback chain (CDN key → stable thumbnail → gradient), the gate heading behaviour (auto vs. custom), the transcript section (speaker turns, time-code seek links, search box), and the Watch next cards including the end_card: false opt-out.
draft.why_use_it: Recording pages let you gate on-demand webinar content behind a sign-up form so every view becomes a lead. The page is fully server-rendered for search engines and AI assistants, includes a searchable transcript with time-coded links that jump the player to any moment, and suggests related recordings so visitors keep watching. Use recording pages when you want a branded, conversion-ready destination for each piece of video content without building a custom website.

entries.title: Agent portal video player: seek from transcript time codes and search the transcript
entries.summary: On agent portal video pages, clicking any transcript time code or chapter button now seeks the video to that moment and begins playback. A **Search** box (previously hidden) lets viewers type to highlight matching words in the transcript, hide non-matching speaker turns, and see a live match count; **Enter** scrolls to the first match and **Escape** clears it. Seeking behind a gated recording moves focus to the sign-up form and holds the timestamp so playback starts at that point after sign-in.

where.path: Marketing → Media → [recording] → Agent portal video page

entries.use_case: Viewers can jump straight to the moment they care about by clicking a time code in the transcript, and quickly find any spoken word without scrubbing through the video — useful for long keynotes or technical sessions where attendees want a specific answer.

cs_action.note: Ships as a default improvement to the portal video embed; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how attendees or on-demand viewers can navigate long recordings or find specific content in a transcript.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer publishing session recordings with transcripts on agent portal pages.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → [recording] → Agent portal video page
internal.gotchas: Requires the server-side transcript time-code markup from the matching web-api release (lib/sites/agent-page/video-portal.js). YouTube and Vimeo embeds reload at the target second rather than seeking in place.
internal.talk_track: Viewers can now click any line in the transcript to jump straight there, or type a word to find every time it was said — no more scrubbing.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining transcript time-code seeking and the transcript search box available on agent portal video pages.
draft.why_use_it: The agent portal video page pairs a recording with its full transcript so viewers can read along, search for any term, and jump to the exact moment it was spoken. This turns a passive recording into a searchable reference — particularly valuable for technical sessions, training content, or any recording where viewers return to find a specific point.

entries.title: Site nav and sign-in card text now meets contrast requirements against branded primary colours
entries.summary: Text in the site navigation bar and sign-in card automatically picks a legible colour — white, near-black, or black — based on contrast against the event's **Primary** brand colour and its blends over the hero gradient. Previously, all text used white at 90 % opacity, which could fall below 3:1 contrast on lighter primary colours.
entries.use_case: Organizers who use a light or yellow primary brand colour no longer need to manually adjust their site to keep navigation and sign-in text readable; the platform picks a contrasting text colour automatically.

cs_action.note: Default on; no action needed. Customers with custom primary colours may notice text switching from white to dark — this is intentional and correct.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their site nav or sign-in card text is hard to read against their brand colour.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using a Site with a non-dark primary brand colour.
internal.gotchas: Customers who relied on white nav text for aesthetic reasons may see it switch to dark text if their primary colour is light. This is a contrast-compliance fix, not a configurable option.
internal.talk_track: The platform now automatically chooses white or dark text for the nav and sign-in card based on your primary colour, so your site always meets accessibility contrast standards.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should note that nav and sign-in card text colour is chosen automatically for contrast against the Primary brand colour and cannot be overridden manually.

entries.title: Auto-generated caption tracks now split long passages into readable cues
entries.summary: Auto-generated caption tracks previously created one cue per transcript line, which meant whole speaker passages appeared as a single block. Captions are now split into short cues (up to 2 lines of 42 characters, up to 7 seconds each), matching standard subtitle conventions. Existing media is corrected the next time the track is requested — no re-upload needed.
entries.use_case: Attendees watching on-demand recordings now see captions that advance naturally line by line, rather than a wall of text that stays on screen for an entire speaker passage.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic; no action needed. Existing recordings self-correct on next request.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that captions on their recordings show a full paragraph at once instead of scrolling naturally.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using transcription or auto-captions on session recordings.
internal.gotchas: Correction happens lazily on the next public-get request, not in bulk — recordings that have not been viewed since the deploy will still show the old cues until someone opens them.
internal.talk_track: Captions now break into short, readable lines just like broadcast subtitles — no re-upload or regeneration needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that auto-generated caption tracks follow standard subtitle timing (≤2 lines, ≤42 chars, ≤7 s per cue) and that existing recordings are corrected automatically on the next playback request.

entries.title: Accessibility fixes: rich-text error states, survey required-field focus, and portal sign-in landmarks
entries.summary: Three groups of accessibility fixes shipped together. (1) A required rich-text answer that fails validation now shows an inline error message and marks the field as invalid so screen readers announce it. (2) On a live survey, attempting to mark done with unanswered required questions now shows inline errors on each question and moves focus to the first unanswered one instead of only showing a toast; opening a session in the survey also moves focus to the session heading. On a CFP inline disclosure, focus now moves to the first unanswered disclosure question instead of staying on **Continue to review**. (3) The portal sign-in page, magic-link landing page, **Switch Account** page, RSVP page, and email-verification page now each have a proper `main` landmark, making them navigable by landmark in screen readers and assistive technology.

where.path: Submission forms (rich-text fields); Surveys; CFP disclosures; Portal sign-in / magic-link / Switch Account pages

entries.use_case: Customers with accessibility requirements or VPAT commitments can point to these fixes as evidence that screen-reader users and keyboard-only users receive proper error announcements and can navigate portal sign-in pages by landmark.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer raises VPAT, WCAG compliance, or reports that screen-reader users cannot navigate portal sign-in or get error feedback on forms.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with accessibility requirements, government or healthcare contracts, or a stated WCAG 2.1 AA commitment.
internal.gotchas: The live NVDA/VoiceOver reading of aria-description inside the rich-text editor iframe has not yet been verified by a human tester (tracked in SB-11305); the code fix is shipped but a QA pass is still pending.
internal.talk_track: Screen readers now hear inline errors on rich-text and survey questions the moment validation fires, and the portal sign-in pages have proper landmarks so users can jump straight to the main content.

draft.docs_gap: The accessibility guide should note that rich-text (WYSIWYG) fields, live surveys, CFP disclosures, and portal sign-in pages all meet WCAG 2.1 AA error-identification and landmark requirements, and describe what screen-reader users hear when a required field fails validation.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard is built to meet accessibility standards so every attendee, speaker and reviewer can use it regardless of how they interact with a computer. Inline error states, focus management and page landmarks let screen readers announce problems at the right moment and let keyboard users jump directly to the content that needs their attention. These behaviours are tested against WCAG 2.1 AA and documented in the Accessibility Conformance Report.

entries.title: Agenda embed: accessible card names and text that scales with the reader's font size
entries.summary: Agenda session cards now derive their accessible name from their visible content in order (track, format, title, speakers), so screen readers announce what sighted attendees see. Time and room — hidden visually — are included as visually hidden text, and the subsession count reads as "Subsessions (n)". All widget font sizes and line heights now use `max(<px>, rem)` so text grows proportionally when a visitor or host page sets a root font size above 16 px, meeting WCAG 2.5.3 and the text-resize requirement.

where.path: Sessions → Embeds → Agenda embed (published on your website)

entries.use_case: Organizers embedding the agenda on their event website can now tell accessibility auditors that the widget passes WCAG 2.5.3 (label-content-name-mismatch) and the text-resize criterion — important for enterprise customers with accessibility procurement requirements.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically to all customers using the agenda embed; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer raises accessibility compliance, VPAT requirements, or mentions a failed axe or WAVE audit on their event website.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with the agenda embed live on their website, especially enterprise or government customers with accessibility procurement requirements.
internal.gotchas: Pages whose host CSS sets html { font-size } above 16 px will now show proportionally larger widget text — this is the intended WCAG behaviour but may surprise customers who have tightly designed layouts. The change is automatic; there is no toggle.
internal.talk_track: The agenda widget now announces sessions to screen readers in the same order sighted visitors read them, and text grows when a visitor increases their browser font size — two common accessibility audit failures, both fixed.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should note that the agenda widget meets WCAG 2.5.3 (label-content-name-mismatch) and that widget text scales with the host page's root font size.
draft.why_use_it: The agenda embed lets you drop a live, filterable session schedule onto any page of your website without rebuilding it every time the program changes. It inherits your event's tracks, formats, rooms and speaker data automatically, so attendees always see the current agenda. The widget is designed to work for all visitors, including those using screen readers or browser text-size settings.

entries.title: Public speaker profile pages on Marketing agent sites
entries.summary: Marketing agent (content gallery) sites now generate a public **Speaker Profile** page for each attributed speaker — showing name, headline, title, company, bio, headshot, website, LinkedIn and X links, plus their recordings, clips and sessions. A **Speaker Directory** listing page is also available. Organizers can attribute speakers to recordings via the MCP server (`update_recording`) and manage profile fields (`get_speaker_profile` / `set_speaker_profile`). Speakers can opt out by setting **hidden: true** on their profile. JSON-LD (ProfilePage, Person, VideoObject actor/contributor) and sitemap entries are generated automatically. Only PII-safe fields are published; email, phone and address are never exposed.

where.path: Marketing → Pages → Content Gallery → Speaker Profiles

entries.use_case: Organisations that publish on-demand recording libraries can now give each speaker a branded public profile page — linking their bio, headshot and social handles to every recording and session they appear in — so visitors can discover more content from speakers they enjoy and speakers get a shareable presence tied to the event.

cs_action.note: Speaker profiles are generated automatically for any attributed speaker on a public content gallery. CS should confirm customers understand the privacy model (opt-out via hidden: true, PII allowlist) and that attribution currently requires the MCP server or API — there is no admin UI for attribution yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about publishing speaker bios or building a speaker directory alongside their on-demand recording library, or when they want better SEO for their content gallery.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Content Galleries (agent sites) who want to surface speaker identity alongside recordings — particularly those running large webinar libraries or conference on-demand hubs.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Pages → Content Gallery → (speaker profile route /speakers/{slug})
internal.gotchas: Attribution is currently only writable via the MCP server (update_recording) or the internal API — there is no point-and-click UI in the admin. Opted-out contacts (hidden: true) are silently dropped from all recording speaker lists, including the gallery snapshot names. Presigned (expiring) image URLs and rejected headshots are never published. Only contacts belonging to the org can be attributed.
internal.talk_track: Your recording library now gives every speaker their own public profile page — bio, headshot, social links and a list of everything they've presented. Visitors can discover more content from speakers they like, and speakers get a shareable URL. It's all driven by the contacts already in your Speaker CRM, with a strict privacy allowlist so only safe fields are ever published.

draft.docs_gap: The recording-pages guide should add a section explaining how to attribute speakers to recordings (via the MCP server or API), how to manage speaker profile fields (bio, photo, links), the opt-out mechanism, and how the speaker directory and individual profile pages are generated and structured.
draft.why_use_it: Speaker profile pages let your content gallery do more than host recordings: each attributed speaker gets a dedicated public page with their bio, headshot, title, company and social links, automatically connected to every recording and session they appear in. Visitors who enjoy a talk can explore everything else that speaker has contributed, and speakers get a shareable URL they can point to from LinkedIn or their own site. Search engines index each profile as a structured Person with VideoObject credits, improving discoverability for both the speaker and your event content. A speaker directory page gives visitors a single place to browse all the speakers in your gallery.

entries.title: Public API exposes speaker profile read and write endpoints
entries.summary: Two new endpoints are available on the public API for speaker profiles on agent sites: `GET /v1/marketing/content/speakers/:contactId` retrieves a speaker's profile, and `PUT /v1/marketing/content/speakers/:contactId` updates bio, photo, title, company, website, LinkedIn, X handle, and the **Hidden** (opt-out) flag. Both endpoints are also available under the org-scoped `/v1/organization/:orgId/marketing/content/` path. The write endpoint requires the `write:marketing` token scope.
entries.use_case: Teams building custom agent sites or integrations can now read and update speaker profile data — including bio, headshot, social links, and opt-out status — programmatically, without requiring manual edits inside Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Additive API change; no existing behaviour is altered. Customers using the public API with read:marketing or write:marketing scopes gain access automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about syncing speaker profiles from an external CMS, website, or custom agent site to Sessionboard via API.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with developer resources who manage speaker content in external systems and want to keep Sessionboard in sync programmatically.
internal.gotchas: The write endpoint requires a token with the write:marketing scope; read:marketing is sufficient for GET. The hidden field controls speaker opt-out visibility on agent sites, not the main program.
internal.talk_track: If you manage speaker bios or headshots outside Sessionboard, you can now push updates directly via the API — including letting speakers opt out of appearing on your agent site.

draft.docs_gap: The API changelog and reference should document the two new speaker profile endpoints (get_speaker_profile and set_speaker_profile), their request/response shapes, required scopes, and the meaning of the hidden opt-out field.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard public API lets you build integrations, automate workflows, and sync data between Sessionboard and your own systems. With speaker profile endpoints, you can keep speaker bios, headshots, and social links consistent across your website, event app, and other tools without manual copy-paste. The `hidden` flag also lets you respect speaker opt-outs from your own systems.

entries.title: Agent pages: BreadcrumbList structured data follows the visible breadcrumb nav, with a configurable per-site root
entries.summary: The `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD on agent pages (recording pages, content galleries, clip pages, and any other agent-rendered page) now mirrors the breadcrumb trail visitors actually see. When a page includes a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` element, each link in that nav becomes a crumb in the structured data, with the page's real title (bound recording or event name) always used as the final item. For sites hosted under a customer's own domain, a per-site **breadcrumb root** can be set via the `edit_site` MCP tool (`site.update { breadcrumbs: { root: [...] } }`), prepending up to five custom links before the site home and list page when no visible nav is present.

where.path: Agent-rendered pages (recording pages, content galleries, clip pages)

entries.use_case: Organisations that embed their Sessionboard recording or gallery pages under their own website domain can now ensure that Google's rich results and AI-powered search answers show the correct breadcrumb trail — matching the navigation visitors see — rather than a generic site-name path. Setting a custom root via the MCP tool lets the trail read "Home → Product webinars → Recording title" instead of just "Site name → Recording title".

cs_action.note: The visible-nav behaviour is automatic for any agent page that already has a breadcrumb nav. The per-site root requires the customer or a staff member to call edit_site via MCP; there is no UI path yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their recording or gallery pages show the wrong breadcrumb trail in Google Search Console or AI-generated answers, or when they host their agent site under their own domain and want the breadcrumb to reflect their site hierarchy.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who publish recording pages, content galleries or clip pages under a custom domain and care about SEO structured data or AI search visibility.
internal.staff_path: MCP tool: edit_site { ops: [{ op: "site.update", breadcrumbs: { root: [{ name, url }] } }] }
internal.gotchas: The per-site root is set only via the MCP tool (edit_site); there is no admin UI. The root accepts at most 5 https links; http links are dropped silently. Pages without a visible breadcrumb nav and without a configured root fall back to the previous behaviour (recording pages keep today's trail; other pages get none).
internal.talk_track: If your recording or gallery pages live under your own website, the breadcrumb Google shows in search results now matches what visitors see on the page. You can also set a custom root so the trail starts from your homepage rather than the Sessionboard site name.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the breadcrumb root setting, how to set it via the MCP edit_site tool, the five-link limit, and how the visible nav drives the JSON-LD trail on recording and gallery pages.
draft.why_use_it: Recording pages, content galleries and clip pages include `BreadcrumbList` structured data so that search engines and AI-powered answer surfaces can display the correct navigation trail alongside your content in results. When your agent site lives under your own domain, accurate breadcrumbs help visitors understand where a page sits within your wider site before they click. The per-site root setting lets you prepend your own site's top-level links so the trail reads naturally from your homepage down to the individual recording.
